edges.description: The steps between the variant and loss of cone function are unknown. The authors of the defining report propose a role for PITPNM3 in phototransduction by analogy with rdgB.
Cone dysfunction is accompanied over time by thinning of the macula, where cones are concentrated. Whether functional loss precedes structural loss has not been shown.
Reduced cone ERG response in both heterozygous and homozygous mice, milder than in patients.
edges.limitations: The allele is p.Val367Met, not the p.Gln626His variant that defines CORD5, and the paper's citation for a human CORD5 patient with p.Val367Met is unresolved in its text. The deficit is milder than in patients, and the line carries rd1 contamination.

edges.description: Structural degeneration appears only in homozygotes, as widespread photoreceptor loss with outer nuclear layer disorganization and, in some animals, retinal detachment. Heterozygotes, the genotype that matches the human disease, keep normal retinal architecture at one year.
edges.limitations: The degeneration is in the homozygous genotype, which does not correspond to the heterozygous human disease, and it is panretinal photoreceptor loss and detachment, not a macular cone lesion; mice have no macula. The line carries rd1 contamination, which confounds attributing the homozygous degeneration to PITPNM3. The allele is p.Val367Met, not p.Gln626His.

evidence.snippet: Here we refine the CORD5 locus previously mapped to 17p13 from 27 to 14.3 cM and identified a missense mutation, Q626H in the phosphatidylinositol transfer (PIT) membrane-associated protein (PITPNM3) (MIM 608921) in two Swedish families.

evidence.snippet: Thus, mutations in PITPNM3 do not appear to be a major cause of cone or cone-rod dystrophy.

nodes.description: Heterozygous c.1878G>C (p.Gln626His) in PITPNM3. PITPNM3 lacks the N-terminal phosphatidylinositol transfer domain of rdgB, and the variant sits in the C-terminal region that interacts with PYK2. Whether the variant weakens PYK2 binding, or acts by haploinsufficiency or a dominant-negative effect, has not been tested, so no functional impact category or activity modifier is recorded.

nodes.description: Knock-in mice carrying a PITPNM3 missense allele, followed to 52 weeks. Both heterozygotes and homozygotes show a reduced cone ERG response, milder than in patients. Outcome on histology depends on genotype: heterozygotes, the genotype that matches CORD5, keep normal retinal architecture at one year, whereas homozygotes develop photoreceptor degeneration with outer nuclear layer disorganization, and a subset of them develop retinal detachment. The authors report contamination of the line with rd1 retinal degeneration mutations, which confounds attributing the homozygous degeneration to PITPNM3.
Acuity declines to legal blindness in early adulthood.
